newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee trims losses as roasters buy on dips.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee trims losses as roasters buy on dips.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Tuesday morning's session near intraday highs after light roaster buying on the dips pared some early losses.
Traders said nearby positions opened slightly higher in line with market expectations but slipped back into negative territory on speculative selling.
By the midday break, the most-active January contract stood $9 lower at $1,421 a tonne after ranging between $1,415 and $1,435. Volume was a thin 1,701 lots.
Traders said the contract now looked safe above the key $1,415 support level.
Conditions were expected to remain dull on lack of fresh market-moving news, they said, noting that many operators are away attending the Sintercafe trade gathering in Costa Rica.
New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said late on Monday that 1,500 60-kg bags of coffee were pending grading at its warehouses.
But traders said the news which came after the London market was closed had no immediate reaction. "That won't affect London," said one.
Broker GNI said the coffee pending grading was small.
"(It) does not represent any real sign that the threat of a squeeze on the (CSCE) December contract had been averted," GNI said in its daily market commentary.
News that Brazil exported 1.89 million bags of coffee in October -- the highest volume since September 1993 -- was within expectations and had no market impact.
Elsewhere, Ugandan coffee authorities said national coffee output could fall to between 3.6 and 3.8 million bags in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) from 4.2 million due to bad weather and disease.
Uganda is Africa's top coffee grower.
